Ravensburger Cozy Retreat 500 Piece Large Format Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 14967 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly I have not done puzzles for years, but recently thought I might like to start again. My first puzzle was 1000 piece and to be honest with you, it was a little frustrating. My eyes aren’t what they used to be and the size of the puzzle was hard for me to work because of the table it was on. I had to stand up a lot to get to the top of the puzzle to work so it just wasn’t relaxing, this time I decided on the 500 piece and I bought this one without realizing the pieces were larger. I am working this on a puzzle mat and it is actually working out the size of 1000 piece puzzle because of the larger pieces. Just be aware of that if you have a smaller place to work your puzzles. So far I am finding this puzzle to be very relaxing and enjoyable there are enough objects in the puzzle so you can get a pretty good idea of where the pieces are going to go in the general area of the puzzle. The pieces are going together very nicely, and there was absolutely no puzzle dust whatsoever in the box.
I would definitely recommend this puzzle especially if you are just getting into puzzles or don’t want one that is very hard. This wouldn’t be considered extremely easy I don’t think but if you are looking for a challenge, I think this one might be a little too casual but for me just getting back into puzzles after years it’s been a very good choice. I’ve been working on it for a few hours today and I have a nice amount completed.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Cozy Retreat 500 Piece Large Format Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 14967 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

Adora Amazing Girls 18 Doll (Amazon Exclusive), Jacqueline One of the things that I love about the Adora dolls is that each doll has her own face sculpt. The dolls look unique and not like clones with different skin tones and face paint.

The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. This allows for a greater range of neck & head motion over other dolls of this size, which have completely cloth torsos and limited, if any, neck motion.

Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

Her mouth is a unique shape and expression, not common with dolls in this space. Her shoes are cute, and her hair is very shiny.

The warning goes on to say however that the kit conforms to federal standards and is only a problem if eaten or chewed. You obviously don't want your kids to eat beads and stuff, and you may want to give this kit to a child who isn't bad about putting things in their mouth regardless.

That said, these kits are made for kids eight and up but honeslty, I think they should be marketed for any person 8 and up, since adults may like to try some of these crafts too. The kits are fun and easy to understand but may be complicated for some. The takeaway though is that the items available in this kit are available inexpensively a any craft store or large retailer and once you have completed the projects in the kit you can refill to keep making and designing them. These are a teaching tool after all but you can learn skills that you can use for years to come and these are all great. A little parental guidance for those who give to a preteen child and it will be OK. All the materials in this kit is decent quality.

The setup for each challenge takes the longest than any other logic puzzle because you have to tear the balls of putty off each color. text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone This is so awesome and it works! I thought that with how affordable it is, that it wouldn't even be able to get off the ground, but it flies great! I have to warn you that it's super hard to fly, though. This will frustrate pretty much everyone except for someone who's already an expert in quad copters. But, it's an awesome first copter to practice on. I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. If you want more control, though, then you should get the CX-10. Or, you should get both, since their parts are all interchangeable.

text_fidelity_a: OYEFLY Squishy Toy Soft Exquisite Horror Doll Scented Stress Relief Toy Soft Toy Kawaii Collection Slow Rising Toy Decompression SimulationToys Cure Toy for Kid Gift Toys Well, I'm almost at a loss for words.  I had started my review on this wonderful little squishy toy - or at least I thought it was wonderful.  I was saying how fun it was and how these squishy toys are great for stress relief (which they are), and how it kind of smelled like vanilla or egg nog.  I thought it was such a cute little doll.  And I was going to mention that I still wouldn't let pets play with it since there were some tiny excess pieces at the seams that were coming loose.  And I started looking closer at the seam that extended all the way around the middle of the toy, as I lowered one of the arms to inspect the seam where the head and arm met, that area just started coming apart.  And it only took minimal pressure for it to continue to rip.  So then I looked at the same area where the head and shoulder/arm met on the other side, and the same thing happened. text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.
text_fidelity_b: Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea

text_fidelity_a: Doggie Doo Corgi Game - Unpredictable Action - Feed The Doggie and Collect His Doo to Win - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This type of thing isn't usually my cup of tea and I typically dislike potty humor. This looked like something to bring humor on the days that my guys aren't getting along, though. It is on the weird side(even thought so from my 3 boys), with all the noises, but it is also on the humorous side. To play, you stick a bit of slime("food") into the bone. The players take turns rolling the die and squeezing the bone the amount rolled. Each player has a shovel that they place behind the dog to catch the "doos" before squeezing the bone. Each time the dog poos, you have to refill the bone. Once all the slime is gone, the player with the most "doos" wins. Had I known that the game used slime, I never would have gotten it. I've had to throw out too many items ruined from it to want it in my home anymore. We just try to be extra careful when playing. It comes with two bags, but it only takes one to play. The second bag is for if the first gets ruined. It says on the bag that it's non-toxic, but to still wash hands after touching it. When the game works, it's fun and makes us laugh. We've had lots of trouble getting it to work properly, though. Many times it won't seal just right(I guess) and no amount of squeezing the bone will make anything happen. It warns not to put too much, which we've tried not to do, and to also make sure the bone is pushed all the way in, which we've tried to do. It still won't work for us half the time, though, which makes it frustrating. If the slime ever gets stuck, the game does come with a stick to push it out. It also comes with a puzzle, which is a nice bonus. Overall, it's still a fun game.
text_fidelity_b: Doggie Doo Corgi Game - Unpredictable Action - Feed The Doggie and Collect His Doo to Win - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

We're having fun with this kit - the instructional guide is outstanding. I'm happy with my purchase.

Four different gun types, each does different amounts of damage, super fun to switch around.  I like the "pew, pew" laser gun.  There is the ability to turn the sound off if you would like, and the ability to turn the lighting off for a "Stealth" mode that lasts about 30 seconds, so you can sneak up on someone if you are playing in the dark.  The quality of the guns feels very solid, no some flimsy light weight thing.  The chest receivers also have a sensor in the back which a lot of the other laser gun sets lack.  This is a very good laser set, highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries I was so excited to get this drone.  I have flown a pretty nice professional DJI but knew this would not be the same.  It arrived on time and in excellent shape.  First problem was there was only 2 batteries (supposed to be 3).  I charged the batteries (in the garbage charger).  I tried to charge them in my B6 charger but it ready low cell voltage- I should have known then there was an issue.  After assembling everything I took it out and followed the directions to calibrate and sync the drone.  It started up and rose up about 10 feet and started drifting to the right no matter what I did.  I landed it and recalibrated and had the same results.  Then the low battery beeping started.  I landed and changed out batteries (total flight time was less than 5 mins).  The second battery would not even turn on the lights.  Recharged the first battery and in 3 mins the drone crashed with a dead battery.  Charged the second battery again and no go.  So frustrated and disappointed.  I packed it all up and put in for a return.  There are a lot of websites that HIGHLY recommend this drone- I have a feeling they are paid for this as this thing is truly unusable.  The trim functions don't do a darn thing and the batteries are horrible.  Thanks to Amazon for a great hassle free return.
text_fidelity_b: Force1 U45W FPV Drone with Camera for Adults - VR Ready Quadcopter RTF Remote Control Drone with 720p HD Wide Angle Drone Camera, 6 Axis Gyro, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, and 2 Drone Batteries

EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments I used to work in Microbiology and one job in particular pertained to streaking for bacteria and viruses on various types of agar plates. We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

4 cubes butter, softened

½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
